topIssues.title: sdm-net-0: restore permissionless fault proofs (register type-0 game implementation)
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
sdm-net-0 was deployed (op-deployer v0.7.1, alphanet preset) with **only the permissioned game type (1)** registered in the DisputeGameFactory (`0x8Da685576610A0a6DEC74E978aCEF45233563933`, Sepolia) while the manifest declared `fp-permissionless` — leaving the proposer silently unable to propose for 12 days (`gameCount()=0`) and the invalid-proposal canary reverting `NoImplementation(uint32)`. We resolved by dropping the feature and running permissioned (devnets-private#1434; details in core-team#2966 and optimism#21273).

This issue tracks the *restore* path if/when permissionless dispute-game coverage is wanted on this devnet:
1. Register a type-0 (CANNON) implementation on the factory (owner action; align prestates with the deployed op-program)
2. Revert devnets-private#1434 (`fp-permissionless` back on) so proposer/challenger/canary reconfigure
3. Verify: proposer proposes type-0 games, canary creates-and-loses games, dispute-mon tracks them

Parent: #21273.

## Summary

- Preserve terminal `engine_newPayload` statuses before local transaction decoding.
- Track whether payloads are L1-derived, locally sequenced, or remotely received.
- Drop malformed remote payload failures while surfacing local execution-client capability failures.

- Extend `MockEngineClient` and add actor-boundary integration coverage for these cases.

Draft follow-up to #22307. This PR contains the broader engine failure-classification and scheduling work that is intentionally excluded from the original admin payload hash validation fix.

topPRs.title: op-dispute-mon: normalize ZK bond accounting
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Claim

Normalize ZK bond outcomes exactly as `ZKDisputeGame.sol` records them and route complete ZK snapshots through every bond consumer without changing Fault output.

## Base and dependency

PR 4 of 5. Base: `feat/zk-monitor-state`; depends on #22227. This remains production-inert until PR 5 enables ZK caller creation.

Stack order: #22225 → #22226 → #22227 → #22228 → #22229.

## Commits and reading order

1. `5ded2fbe98` adds pinned ZK bond, credit, withdrawal, WETH, balance, and delay reads.
2. `ebfb82995f` validates and normalizes the contract outcome table, then routes ZK through the bond lane.
3. `0e878db050` rejects withdrawal delays that overflow `time.Duration`.

## Review focus

- The pinned read and result-count validation establishes the inputs to the normalization table.
- Self-challenge, invalid-parent burn, refund mode, overlapping roles, and unchallenged `TotalBonds < ChallengerBond` each map directly to a Solidity outcome path.
- Shared-WETH obligations include ZK, ZK maturity is inclusive only after a real request, and Fault credit/collateral/withdrawal/forfeiture behavior remains unchanged.

## Intentional behavior changes

- Configured address zero is excluded from honest-actor metrics, so an invalid-parent burn cannot appear as an honest win.
- ZK withdrawal maturity follows the contract's inclusive boundary; Fault retains its existing exclusive boundary.

## Tests

- `mise exec -- go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts ./op-dispute-mon/... -count=1`
- `mise exec -- go test -race ./op-dispute-mon/mon/... -count=1`
- `mise exec -- just lint-go`

topPRs.title: op-alloy,op-reth: report zero DA footprint on PostExec receipts
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Follow-up to #22219, which excluded PostExec (`0x7D`) transactions from `op-core/fees.CalcDAFootprint`. That closed the Go-side block-total recomputation; this closes the remaining receipt gap and adds the regression coverage neither change had.

Specification: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/926

## The receipt gap

Jovian repurposes the receipt's `blobGasUsed` field to carry the transaction's DA footprint ([jovian/exec-engine.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/main/specs/protocol/jovian/exec-engine.md#receipts)). op-reth's RPC receipt builder recomputed that value from the transaction bytes for every transaction once Jovian was active, with no type gate, so a `0x7D` reported a non-zero footprint — the Fjord minimum-size floor guarantees at least `100 * daFootprintGasScalar`, never zero.

The block-level accumulator in `alloy-op-evm` already excludes the `0x7D`, and `blobGasUsed` is not a consensus receipt field, so the executor's zero has no path to the RPC layer. Gating the recomputation on the transaction type restores the invariant `sum(receipt.blobGasUsed) == header.blobGasUsed`.

`OpTransaction::is_post_exec` is added as a *provided* method so callers behind the generic bound can test the type without the inherent `OpTxEnvelope::is_post_exec`, which the bound does not expose. Existing implementors, including downstream extended envelopes, compile unchanged.

## Shared helper

`op_revm::da_footprint_gas(encoded, scalar)` now holds the footprint arithmetic, which was duplicated across the block executor, the receipt builder, and two tests. Which transactions are charged stays with each caller, because the layers differ: the block total excludes deposits *and* the `0x7D`, while a receipt reports zero only for the `0x7D`.

## Regression coverage

The block-level exclusion was correct but untested. op-geth recomputed the footprint independently and so acted as a cross-check; it is no longer a supported verifier, which leaves the accumulator unguarded. The new `alloy-op-evm` test asserts a `0x7D` leaves `da_footprint_used` unchanged, and also asserts that a *counted* `0x7D` would have moved the total, so it cannot pass vacuously.

End to end, the invariant is asserted in the SDM acceptance suite — Lagoon at genesis with SDM opted in, the only in-tree chain whose blocks contain a `0x7D`. It checks that the `0x7D` receipt reports zero and that the non-deposit receipts still sum to the header's `blobGasUsed`, with a positive total so it cannot pass vacuously. The Jovian suites pin Jovian at genesis (`sysgo.WithJovianAtGenesis` writes an explicit nil offset for every later fork), so Lagoon — and therefore SDM — can never be active there.

## Validation

The receipt test was written first and failed on the baseline with `left: Some(10000)` — exactly `100` (Fjord floor) × `100` (scalar) — then passed after the gate. Re-checked after the Lagoon rename.

- `cargo nextest run --all-features -p op-revm -p op-alloy-consensus -p alloy-op-evm -p reth-optimism-rpc` — 314 passed
- `cargo clippy` on the same crates, `--all-features --all-targets` — no warnings in the changed crates
- `just check-no-std`, `just fmt-check` — clean
- `gofmt`, `go vet ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/sdm/...` — clean

**Not run:** the SDM acceptance assertion itself, which needs a devnet. It is verified as compiling and correct by inspection, not executed.

## Out of scope

Deposit receipts also report a non-zero `blobGasUsed`, even though deposits contribute zero to the block total. specs#926 does not cover it and changing it is a user-visible RPC change, so it is left alone — it is also why `da_footprint_gas` takes bytes and a scalar and leaves the exclusion to its callers.

topPRs.title: alloy-op-evm: synthesize post-exec tx result on replay paths
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
## Description

`debug_traceBlockByNumber` / `debug_traceTransaction` fail with `invalid chain ID` on every block containing an SDM post-exec (0x7d) transaction (ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#163).

**Root cause:** consensus execution never runs 0x7d txs through the EVM — `OpBlockExecutor::execute_transaction_without_commit` short-circuits them with a synthetic no-op success. The RPC trace path, however, replays each transaction directly via `evm.transact`, and the post-exec tx env built by `FromTxWithEncoded<TxPostExec>` inherited `chain_id: Some(1)` from `TxEnv::default()` (revm's builder default is mainnet), which revm's `validate_tx_env` rejects on any other chain. Fixing only the chain id wouldn't help: no honest tx env for a zero-gas-limit transaction with calldata passes revm's intrinsic-gas validation, so the transaction must not be transacted at all.

**Fix:** short-circuit post-exec transactions in `OpEvm::transact_raw`, returning the same consensus-defined no-op result the block executor produces (now shared via `post_exec::noop_post_exec_result`). This covers `debug_trace*` and every other generic replay path for both op-reth and op-reth-premium (whose `PostExecEvmFactoryAdapter` wraps this factory). Tracers see no execution and emit an empty frame — `revm-inspectors` geth builders return `Default::default()` on an empty arena.

Also makes the post-exec `TxEnv` conversion honest (`chain_id: None`, `gas_limit: 0`, payload RLP as calldata) so the env is correct for anything else that inspects it.

## Testing

- `transact_raw_short_circuits_post_exec_tx` (with/without inspector): a post-exec tx on a chain with id ≠ 1 returns success, zero gas, empty state.
- `transact_raw_rejects_mainnet_chain_id_on_other_chain`: control documenting the failure mode the short-circuit avoids.
- `post_exec_tx_env_reflects_transaction_fields`: the conversion no longer leaks mainnet defaults.
- `cargo test -p alloy-op-evm` (70 passed), clippy clean, `reth-optimism-evm` / `reth-optimism-rpc` compile.

Fixes ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#163

topPRs.title: kona-registry: Default chains with no interop config to a self-only dependency set
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
kona's registry build script emitted a `DependencySet` only for chains declaring an `[interop]` block. Every other registry chain, OP Mainnet included, had none — so kona-client's interop boot fell back to a host-supplied depset from the preimage oracle, trusting unverified data inside a proof. The host serves an empty depset when `--depset-cfg` is absent.

An absent `[interop]` section is a single-chain dependency set; the declaration is just omitted for succinctness. op-node and op-supernode already read it that way via `superchain.GetDepset`; kona-client now matches, and the regenerated `etc/depsets.json` covers all 53 registry chains. A custom `depsets.json` that contradicts a registry chain's set now panics, exactly as a conflicting chain list or superchain config entry does.
